candidates.title: Arizona university hockey coach put on paid leave after report on Canadian NHL prospect's collapse
candidates.description: Arizona State University hockey coach Greg Powers has been placed on paid administrative leave after an anonymous letter from teammates of NHL prospect Matthew Mayich disputed aspects of the school's review into the Hamilton-born player's collapse during an outdoor workout last month.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Could the Parti Québécois actually abolish the monarchy in Quebec?
candidates.description: Parti Québécois Leader Paul St-Pierre Plamondon says he wants to defund the office of the lieutenant-governor and pass a law to sever the province's ties to the Crown. But is a phaseout of the monarchy constitutionally feasible in Quebec?
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: After 'doom and gloom' decade, Fort McMurray readies for a boom
candidates.description: The Alberta community synonymous with meteoric oil booms and crippling busts is now staring down another potential wave of economic fortune.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Victory for separatist Parti Québécois would present a new political test for Carney
candidates.description: There is an immediate political test looming for Prime Minister Mark Carney and his government as early as next week, one that has not been on the political radar federally for more than a decade.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: 'Crisis of Indigenous child welfare' continues months after Ont. couple's murder trial: advocate
candidates.description: Halton Indigenous advocate Jody Harbour says a months-long murder trial in Milton, Ont., shone a light on "the continuing crisis of Indigenous child welfare in Ontario." The co-founder of Grandmother's Voice said change means ensuring front-line workers know how to support Indigenous people.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Manitoba Tories wrong to claim unity after caucus minority tried to force removal: Obby Khan
candidates.description: Former Manitoba Progressive Conservative leader Obby Khan says he's dismayed the party is defending its integrity, after he was taken off-guard by caucus members trying to push him out.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Matthew Mayich's Arizona teammates dispute school report on workout before Hamilton NHL prospect's collapse
candidates.description: An anonymous letter by Arizona State University hockey players that was sent to the school's president disputes aspects of ASU's official review into events that led up to Matthew Mayich's collapse. The letter alleges the Hamilton-born NHL prospect "received no water" during the outdoor workout on a hot day last month and calls for an independent investigation.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Carney announces $1.2B in funding to protect oceans as major projects loom
candidates.description: Prime Minister Mark Carney announced $1.2 billion in federal funding for ocean protections Tuesday, as the country moves toward decisions on a new pipeline to the West Coast and the expansion of a major port in Metro Vancouver.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: When the Manitoba PCs lost their leader, the NDP lost its greatest asset
candidates.description: Obby Khan was to Wab Kinew what Justin Trudeau was to Pierre Poilievre: The gift that kept on giving, as long as he remained in his position. Unfortunately for the NDP, he self-ejected.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: CSIS may have misused power to commit offences while gathering intelligence: watchdog
candidates.description: The Canadian Security Intelligence Service may not have complied with the law when using special powers to gather information, a review by the national spy watchdog has found.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Sask. drone company says no 'special rights' attached to $10M US investment linked to Trump Jr.
candidates.description: Saskatoon-based drone maker Draganfly Inc. is receiving a $10-miilion US "strategic investment" from two U.S. firms, including one linked to Donald Trump Jr., but says there are no board seats or other perks attached to the agreement.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Conservative MP Scott Aitchison expected to resign this fall: sources
candidates.description: MP and former Conservative leadership candidate Scott Aitchison is expected to resign his seat later this fall, sources tell CBC News.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Are the raspberries in my fridge OK to eat? What to know about chemical levels on Driscoll's berries
candidates.description: You may be having second thoughts about eating the berries in your fridge after CBC News spoke with a whistleblower who made a startling claim about the amount of chemicals on fruit that a U.S. company allegedly shipped to Canada.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Alberta, Anglican diocese accept vicarious liability in lawsuit over alleged 1980s sexual assaults
candidates.description: The Alberta government and the Anglican Synod of the Diocese of Edmonton have admitted vicarious liability for an Anglican priest's alleged sexual assaults against youths in a city jail in the 1980s.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Premier Scott Moe goes big on nuclear with plans to explore 2 large nuclear reactors in northwest Sask.
candidates.description: Saskatchewan says it wants to have a large nuclear reactor online by 2042. It has also narrowed down the location of further study for its construction of Small Modular Reactors (SMR) to the Rafferty site near Estevan.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: 'It's devastating': Hundreds of Stelco workers in Hamilton and Nanticoke face uncertain future due to layoffs
candidates.description: Hundreds of Stelco workers in Hamilton and Nanticoke, Ont. are facing an uncertain future after the company announced it will indefinitely idle its cold-rolled and coated operations at its Hamilton Works plant.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Judge tosses drug trafficking convictions for B.C. compassion club founders after constitutional challenge
candidates.description: A B.C. Supreme Court judge has ruled in favour of two harm reduction activists convicted of drug trafficking who argued they were doing it to reduce the harms caused by toxic drugs.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Passengers foil bid to crash Dubai-Tel Aviv flight after co-pilot stabbed pilot, Israel says
candidates.description: Passengers on a FlyDubai flight reached Israel safely on Wednesday after passengers and crew foiled a co-pilot's attempt to crash the aircraft, Israeli officials said, in a struggle that began when he stabbed the pilot and sent the jet plunging.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Why pro-Trump ads — paid for with public money — are airing on U.S. TV
candidates.description: With crucial midterm elections just weeks away, the White House is using taxpayer funds to air campaign-style TV ads featuring U.S. President Donald Trump.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: G20 trade ministers are meeting in Wisconsin. Many will be discussing deals without their U.S. host
candidates.description: Most of the officials attending the G20 trade ministers' meeting in Milwaukee, Wisc., find themselves in challenging positions, largely because of U.S. President Donald Trump's global tariff agenda. It makes for a potentially unusual summit, with high-level meetings on the sidelines where different countries discuss plans to work around the host.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Tennessee's planned execution of Christa Pike halted pending appeals court review
candidates.description: Pike, now 50, was convicted for a murder she committed at age 18. Her case has renewed debate over the death penalty for young offenders, with supporters arguing Tennessee should consider Pike's age at the time, mental illness and a history of severe sexual abuse.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Russian airstrikes kill at least 7, damage infrastructure in Ukraine
candidates.description: Russia unleashed an air campaign against Ukraine's energy grid on Wednesday, ‌hitting power facilities and infrastructure around Kyiv and other regions in what Ukraine's prime minister said was the heaviest combined attack on energy sites in months.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Eiffel Tower chief to step down after female staff excluded during Hindu delegation visit
candidates.description: The head of the company that runs the Eiffel Tower will step down at the end of the year after female staff at the landmark building in Paris were excluded during a visit by a Hindu religious group.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Polo makes 2nd landfall on Mexico's Pacific coast
candidates.description: Hurricane Polo made a second landfall on Mexico's northwestern Pacific coast on Tuesday after drenching the southern Baja California peninsula.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Princess Diana’s brother says ‘she will never be extinguished’
candidates.description: Charles Spencer has written a new book about the late Princess Diana, and Buckingham Palace is not impressed. In conversation with CBC Radio The Current host Matt Galloway he offers an intimate look at his sister’s character and talks about the tense moments with Prince Charles in the aftermath of the tragic 1997 Paris car crash.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Trump says top tech firms have signed accord to 'self-police' AI development
candidates.description: U.S. President Donald Trump has signed a voluntary pact with artificial intelligence companies to "self-police" the technology's development.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: UN Security Council extends mandate of anti-gang force in Haiti into 2027
candidates.description: The United Nations Security Council on Tuesday extended by six months the mandate of an international security force in Haiti intended to fight powerful armed groups that have taken control of much of the country.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Trump trade adviser says Canada will 'pay even more dearly' if 'you interfere' in U.S. midterms
candidates.description: One of U.S. President Donald Trump's trade advisers is threatening repercussions for Canada if it "interferes" in the upcoming midterm elections — though it's not clear what he anticipates the country would do to impact the vote.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: U.S. Supreme Court says Trump can continue deportations to 3rd countries — for now
candidates.description: The U.S. Supreme Court on Tuesday let President Donald Trump's administration resume deporting migrants to countries other than their own without offering them the chance to show the ‌harms they may face, bolstering a tool his administration has used for rapid expulsions as part of his immigration crackdown.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Did locals help thwart a terror plot in the U.K.? | About That
candidates.description: Avneet Dhillon breaks down what we know about a foiled suspected terror plot near a U.K. air base used by the U.S. in its war on Iran. Images provided by The Canadian Press, Reuters, Adobe Stock and Getty Images
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: ShinyHunters hackers say they won't leak sensitive FBI data
candidates.description: The hacking group behind a massive FBI data breach says it will not publish the information it obtained, but it cannot guarantee what will happen with the data it already shared with journalists.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: British police say no explosives found in vehicles near U.S.-run base
candidates.description: A surprise decision by the U.K.'s counterterrorism police to release five suspects on bail during an investigation into a suspected bomb plot at a U.S.-operated air force base in England has prompted questions and uncertainty about the incident.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: What to know about Cornell's alleged frat house gang-rape case and the 'Cornell 7'
candidates.description: Investigators in New York are reopening an investigation into an alleged gang rape at Cornell University after a woman filed a lawsuit claiming the university didn't do enough to protect her.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Manchester City guilty of nearly 115 charges of financial wrongdoing, Premier League says in explosive verdict
candidates.description: Manchester City has been found guilty of almost all of the unprecedented 115 charges of financial wrongdoing it faced, the Premier League confirmed on Tuesday, in one of the biggest scandals in English soccer history.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: U.S. forces leave Iraq after first arriving in 2003
candidates.description: U.S. forces ended their mission in Iraq on Wednesday, a departure that has been celebrated as a victory by Iran and its allies, who now have deep influence in the country where 4,500 Americans died during more than two decades of war.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Heavy rains in Thailand kill 23, cause airport chaos
candidates.description: The death toll from rains and flooding in Thailand has risen ‌to 23, authorities said on Tuesday Waters receded from the hard-hit capital Bangkok, where its main airport operated in chaos and the government approved a multi-million aid package.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Stelco's U.S. owner to face 'fullest extent of the law' over layoffs: PM Carney
candidates.description: Prime Minister Mark Carney says the federal government will use "all powers" at its disposal to pursue Stelco's American owners "to the fullest extent of the law."
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Deloitte Canada cuts GDP growth forecast by 20% as tariffs grip economy amid Trump's trade war
candidates.description: Deloitte Canada has shaved 20 per cent off its growth forecast for Canada's economy in 2027, citing increasingly tough conditions for consumers and businesses. The accounting firm's latest outlook comes as a new American ban on select Canadian imports took effect.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: LNG Canada to move forward with Phase 2 expansion project in Kitimat, B.C.
candidates.description: LNG Canada says its multibillion-dollar Phase 2 expansion in Kitimat, B.C., is going forward, in a move that could double exports of liquefied natural gas from the northern coastal facility to overseas markets.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: U.S. bans on Canadian booze hit producers on one of trade war's thorniest fronts
candidates.description: As of Tuesday, some Canadian products, including dairy, motorcycles and alcohol, can no longer cross the border to the U.S. at all, thanks to an American import ban. It's the latest escalation in the Canada-U.S. trade war, where booze has taken centre stage.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: OpenAI scraps release of new AI model over safety concerns
candidates.description: OpenAI has scrapped the release of GPT-6.1 Astra, a next-generation artificial intelligence model planned for an October debut, after internal testing found the system did not meet the company's ‌safety and alignment standards, the ChatGPT maker confirmed on Monday.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Six smugglers jailed for manslaughter over worst Channel small boats disaster
candidates.description: Thirty-one migrants died when their boat went down in November 2021. The trial found that the guilty men were part of two smuggling networks.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Russia launches largest attack on Ukraine energy infrastructure since spring
candidates.description: In total 11 regions of the country were attacked overnight, with residential buildings and railways also targeted, the Ukrainian PM says.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Last UK and US troops leave Iraq as anti-Islamic State mission ends
candidates.description: The withdrawal of coalition forces, under a deal agreed two years ago, was a key demand of the Iraqi government.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Girl has multiple surgeries to control infections after strike in Gaza
candidates.description: Witnesses say Raseel's tent was hit by an Israeli helicopter strike. Israel’s military says it has no record of the attack.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: US actor Chad Lowe 'heartbroken' by death of daughter Fiona aged 13
candidates.description: Lowe and his wife Kim Painter announce the death of their daughter, who "was the light of our lives".
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Chinese AI tool told researchers how to make bioweapons
candidates.description: Mindgard said it discovered in July that Kimi models K2.6 and K3 Swarm could evade developer's safety limits.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: 'He will never walk free': Indian judge's letter promises child sex abuse survivor
candidates.description: In the emotional letter, the judge describes the survivor as "the bravest little girl this court has ever seen".
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Restaurant named after Xi Jinping attacked by Chinese nationals in South Korea
candidates.description: The owner said he chose the name because he wanted to run the "best Chinese restaurant" in South Korea.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Three takeaways from Trump's 'Super Intelligence' summit
candidates.description: The meeting at the White House came as some tech bosses and experts have called for tighter rules around AI.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: 'I was lured into a trap': Evan Gershkovich on moment that led to 16 months in Russian jail
candidates.description: The US journalist says he realised he was a "a pawn in a greater game" when he was not interrogated or tortured by FSB agents.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Ukraine's prized steel industry left in ruins by Russian missile campaign
candidates.description: Ukraine's remaining steelworks, a vital part of its economy, have all but ground to a halt because of relentless attacks.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Couple describes relief at rescue after whale destroys their yacht
candidates.description: Jeremy and Gemma Cooper were 500 miles off the coast of New Zealand when their yacht, the Tai Tam, collided with a sperm whale.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Luxury prison in Indonesia demolished after public outcry
candidates.description: Indonesian lawmakers on Wednesday ordered the demolition of a controversial luxury compound inside a penitentiary near the capital.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Watch: Moment a government building collapses into a river in Nepal amid floods
candidates.description: The municipality building in Baglung was left teetering on an unstable ledge due to floods before it fell into a river.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Close-up look at Turner's '£50m' Rome painting on show in the city
candidates.description: Turner’s early 19th century painting - Rome, from Mount Aventine - will be on display in the Italian capital for the first time ahead of an auction in London in December.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Meet 'Backpack', the chunky bear who won Fat Bear Week
candidates.description: The brown bear, described by one supporter as having both the "chonk and the badonk", will shortly enter hibernation, which can last up to six months.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Warning more homes will be uninsurable due to flood risk
candidates.description: Aviva boss Amanda Blanc said England was "for sure" building homes that might be uninsurable at some point in the future.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Watch: Bangkok locals create floating market during floods
candidates.description: As sellers waded through floodwaters to sell produce like fish and vegetables from floating platforms and foam boxes, buyers walked or paddled between the makeshift stalls to buy their groceries.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Lives 'will be lost' unless UK does more to combat wildfires, committee chairwoman says
candidates.description: Baroness Brown says there must be better training and planning, after a record year for wildfires in England and Wales.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Greetings from Syria, where time seems to melt as a glassmaker braves scorching temps
candidates.description: As a Syrian glassmaker created his wares in Damascus, watching his craft reminded this reporter to slow down and enjoy the moment.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: How Ukrainians are coping with new, more deadly Russian attacks
candidates.description: Zanny Minton Beddoes, The Economist's editor in chief , just visited Ukraine. She says, despite all its drone weaponry, Kyiv is under extraordinary bombardment, as Russia tries to make it unlivable.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: A pilot stabs another pilot and tries to crash their flight to Tel Aviv, Israel says
candidates.description: As the plane went into a spin and began to plunge, a passenger and crew members got into the cockpit, subdued the pilot and diverted the flight to land in Saudi Arabia, Israel's leader says.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: U.S. forces exit Iraq amid Iran war. And, SCOTUS revives Trump deportation policy
candidates.description: The U.S. has withdrawn its final troops from Iraq, leaving its defense future uncertain. And, the Supreme Court has sided for now with the Trump administration on third-country deportations.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: The U.S. military withdraws from Iraq over 2 decades after its invasion
candidates.description: 23 years after the United States military invaded Iraq, sparking an insurgency and a civil war, the U.S. has withdrawn its forces, as the country still tries to combat Iranian influence.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Retired general who led troops in Iraq warns U.S. exit may give Iran, ISIS an opening
candidates.description: Retired Lt. Gen. H.R. McMaster, who commanded U.S. troops in Iraq, says the withdrawal could strengthen Iran and leave Iraq more vulnerable to ISIS.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: An 87-year-old woman whose eviction sparked protests in Spain is returning home
candidates.description: María del Carmen Abascal's case has drawn tens of thousands of people to the streets in recent days and led the Spanish government to present measures to address the country's housing crisis.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Potential Taiwan tension sparked 'last minute' change in Trump-Xi National Archives visit
candidates.description: The sudden change was precipitated because of Chinese displeasure over one document that the U.S. had planned to show.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Trump weakens fuel efficiency standards. And, Cornell fraternity rape case reopened
candidates.description: The Trump administration has weakened fuel efficiency standards for new cars. And, prosecutors have reopened a Cornell University fraternity rape case.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: As the U.S. signals a smaller Middle East footprint, Turkey is ready to step in
candidates.description: Turkey's bid for regional influence comes as the Middle East has been hit by profound shocks that started with the Hamas-led 2023 attack on Israel and continue with the seven-month-old war on Iran.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: A startup wants to build a massive nuclear-powered data center on public land in Utah
candidates.description: Valar Atomics wants to place over 450 reactors on more than 9,500 acres in Utah to power a huge data center project.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: One year after the end of the EV tax credit, is the future still electric?
candidates.description: Congress got rid of a $7,500 federal tax credit for new electric vehicle buyers. One year later, are people still buying EVs?
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: How to hide your spending habits from retailers (so you don't get ripped off)
candidates.description: Companies have changed the way they price their products — and shoppers are getting deliberately overcharged. Here are steps you can take to ensure you are getting the best deal.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Democrat Pete Buttigieg criticizes Trump's rollback of fuel-economy standards
candidates.description: The former transportation secretary says weaker fuel-economy standards could raise long-term costs for drivers and leave U.S. automakers further behind China.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: News organizations ask court to bar White House enforcement of access ban
candidates.description: Three news outlets that President Trump banished from White House grounds asked a federal court to block the ban until the case is resolved.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: After failed execution, health workers say Tennessee's method flouts medical ethics
candidates.description: After a botched lethal injection in May, dozens of Tennessee medical professionals told the governor that healthcare professionals shouldn't help with executions, no matter the method.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Travel plans? Here's what to know as measles exposures reach trains and games
candidates.description: Measles is traveling, with outbreaks in Pennsylvania, Ohio and New York, and exposures on transportation and in sports. What should you know before getting on a plane or train?
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: What's behind HHS claims that gender-affirming care 'may' radicalize
candidates.description: The report is the agency's latest effort to chip away at trust in established health care models for transgender people. Critics say it frames transgender identity as illegitimate or even dangerous.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Montana starts enforcing Medicaid work requirements on Oct 1. Patients are confused
candidates.description: In most states, people with Medicaid coverage will have to prove they're working, volunteering or studying, starting Jan. 1. But Montana is starting that early, and it's sowing confusion and anxiety.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: They were promised protection. Instead, these kids with disabilities died in foster care
candidates.description: Disabled kids make up the largest group in foster care. They have the worst outcomes. They stay in foster care longest. They're the most likely to die.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Drugs are widely used to sedate dementia patients. Her sons wanted to keep her off them
candidates.description: Potent sedating medications are often used on agitated people with dementia in long-term care facilities despite federal efforts to discourage them. A clash over whether to drug a Michigan woman illuminates the wrenching decisions families and guardians face.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Rural voters support MAHA movement, but feel little impact, poll finds
candidates.description: A new poll from KFF-AP shows that rural voters support the Make America Healthy Again movement, but they don't think it's had a positive impact on their lives.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: This startup wants to prove gene-editing embryos is safe for making healthy babies
candidates.description: Origin Genomics aims to prove that the potential benefits of its technology for editing disease-causing genes in human embryos outweigh the risks.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: This year's MacArthur Fellows include researchers who fuse science and justice
candidates.description: The MacArthur Foundation has just announced its latest batch of 20 fellows. Among the recipients of the $800,000 "no-strings-attached" fellowships are researchers who were recognized for their work at the intersection of science and justice.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Tennessee's failed execution ignites a medical ethics debate
candidates.description: After a botched lethal injection in May, dozens of Tennessee medical professionals told the governor that healthcare professionals shouldn't help with executions, ever. No matter the method.

candidates.title: Skill-Space Shooting for Autonomous Robot Policy Improvement
candidates.description: Robots deployed in the physical world must be able to improve beyond their initial training as they encounter new situations and failures. For this improvement to scale across tasks, it must make effective use of experience without requiring human demonstration of each correction. Recent agentic systems offer a way to reduce this reliance on human effort by using foundation models to autonomously compose learned behaviors to complete tasks. Yet completing tasks this way does not itself teach a task policy to overcome its own failures; that requires turning these behaviors into learnable corrections for the policy. Our insight is that many such corrections are familiar short behaviors, or skills: they recur across tasks and describe actions that foundation models can reason about from a scene. We introduce skill-space shooting, which uses foundation model guidance to explore corrections through these reusable skills and turn successful trials into policy improvement. Real-world experiments show repeated improvement in policies acting autonomously, while skills can also be shared to reduce the teaching needed to improve on new tasks. By making reusable skills a source of corrective supervision, skill-space shooting enables scalable and generalizable policy improvement within and across tasks. Additional results and videos at https://skill-space-shooting.github.io.
candidates.author: Zihang Rui, Renhao Wang, Haoxu Huang, Yang Gao

candidates.title: Imagine3D-LLM: Teaching MLLMs to Imagine 3D Scenes Before Answering
candidates.description: Reasoning about the 3D world from multi-view images remains a fundamental challenge for Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs). While modern MLLMs handle single-image inputs effectively, they struggle to integrate evidence across viewpoints into a coherent 3D understanding. A growing body of work attempts to close this gap by injecting 3D awareness into MLLMs, either by boosting fine-grained pixel-level cross-view correspondence or by fusing features from 3D geometry foundation models, yet a substantial gap to human reasoning persists. In this work, we revisit human spatial reasoning, which suggests that rather than relying on fine-grained geometry cues, humans roughly identify common objects across views, infer the relative geometry between viewpoints, and assemble a coarse 3D layout of the scene. Inspired by this process, we introduce Imagine3D-LLM, an MLLM that learns to assemble a similar compact 3D representation of the scene and conditions its answer on this representation. Concretely, we append a small set of learnable summary tokens after the image tokens, decode them into a compact 3D Gaussian Splatting representation supervised by a photometric reconstruction loss, and train jointly with the standard next-token prediction objective. Notably, although only the summary tokens receive direct reconstruction supervision, this objective also induces stronger cross-frame correspondence within the LLM's underlying image features, suggesting that learning to reconstruct propagates 3D-aware signals throughout the model. As a result, Imagine3D-LLM consistently outperforms prior approaches across multiple spatial reasoning and 3D understanding benchmarks, suggesting that imagining the scene can be more effective than being told its pixel-wise geometry.
candidates.author: Jaewoo Jung, Hyeonseo Yu, Honggyu An, Jisang Han, Mungyeom Kim, Minkyeong Jeon, Heeseong Shin, Wonjun Moon, Federico Tombari, Daniel Barath, Marc Pollefeys, Seungryong Kim, Sunghwan Hong

candidates.title: In-context Robot Learning Made Simple: A Democratized Recipe for Manipulation Tasks
candidates.description: We study robotic in-context learning (ICL), an emerging paradigm that enables robots to infer and execute tasks from visual demonstrations. Despite its growing promise, the problem itself remains under-defined: a visual demonstration simultaneously conveys action trajectories, object semantics, manipulation affordances, spatial relations, and task goals, making it unclear what information the robot is actually expected to follow. In this work, we first provide a clear problem definition of robot ICL that explicitly defines its learning target and resolves this fundamental prompt ambiguity. Building on this definition, we develop a minimalist and reproducible ICL framework (SimpleICL) with a visual prompt encoder and a low-cost data collection protocol. Without massive pre-training or specialized data infrastructure, our framework achieves strong performance in both simulation and real-world environments. Extensive experiments further reveal several key properties of robot ICL, including action, semantic, composition, and affordance discrimination. We will fully open-source our data and training pipeline to facilitate systematic and reproducible research on robot ICL. The project page can be found at https://simpleicl.github.io/simpleicl.
candidates.author: Minxing Li, Minghao Han, Weizhi Zhao, Hanwen Wang, Xiangshuo Liu, Shuyao Shang, Jingxiang Zhou, Mingchao Sun, Hongyu Pan, Mu Xu, Yu Liu, Lue Fan, Zhaoxiang Zhang

candidates.title: Counterfactual Video Generation Enables Scalable Humanoid Loco-Manipulation
candidates.description: Teaching humanoids loco-manipulation skills, such as carrying diverse objects, via visual imitation is a promising path toward generalist robots. However, collecting diverse, high-quality interaction videos, such as clips that clearly show a person's full body and unoccluded interactions with objects, poses a practical barrier to scaling this approach. We propose PRISM, a real-to-sim-to-real framework that overcomes this limitation by amplifying a handful of real videos into a large, diverse training set. PRISM first generates hundreds of diverse "counterfactual" human-object interaction videos via video-to-video (V2V) generation from a few exemplar real videos. Our contact-anchored real-to-sim pipeline then reconstructs both human and object motions, retargeting this imperfect video data into physically plausible trajectories. The intra-class variability across these counterfactual videos lets us train a single policy that generalizes to unseen objects within each category. We demonstrate the full pipeline by deploying this policy on a real robot without any real-world fine-tuning. Using only onboard depth observations, our humanoid picks up, carries, and drops objects, including boxes, barrels, bins, and balls, across novel instances, sizes, and initial configurations.
candidates.author: Zihan Wang, Zhen Wu, Pieter Abbeel, Rocky Duan, Jitendra Malik, Carmelo Sferrazza, C. Karen Liu, Guanya Shi, Angjoo Kanazawa

candidates.title: STEPQuant: When and Where Errors Matter in Delta-Rule Recurrent State Quantization
candidates.description: Linear attention replaces growing KV caches with fixed-size recurrent states, yet these persistent states can become a substantial memory bottleneck under concurrent serving. Directly quantizing recurrent states to low precision often leads to severe accuracy degradation, as quantization errors propagate through successive state updates. We discover that the impact of these errors depends on two complementary dimensions: temporally, errors in long-lived memory can persist across many decoding steps; spatially, errors in different key rows affect model outputs differently, while state magnitudes vary substantially along both rows and columns. Motivated by these observations, we propose STEPQuant, a spatial-temporal post-training quantization framework for Delta-rule recurrent states. STEPQuant allocates precision according to error magnitude and memory lifetime, and jointly fits key-row and value-column scales based on state distributions and key-row impact on output error. Experiments on Qwen3.8-27B and Kimi-Linear-48B-A3B-Instruct across both long- and short-generation benchmarks show that STEPQuant closely matches FP32-state accuracy under a nominal 6-bit budget and outperforms uniform INT8 in its 4-bit configuration. Integrated into SGLang with optimized GPU kernels, 6-bit STEPQuant achieves over 5x recurrent-state compression and reduces total serving memory by up to 68.7%. Our code is available at https://github.com/Dreamer-Toby/STEPQuant.
candidates.author: Bingchen Yao, Haobo Xu, Haokun Lin, Yichen Wu, Ziyu Guo, Renrui Zhang, Zhichao Lu, Zhenan Sun, Ying Wei

candidates.title: LeapQuant: Efficient Linear Attention with Accurate Recurrent State Quantization
candidates.description: Recent LLMs increasingly adopt hybrid designs that replace standard attention with linear attention, such as Gated DeltaNet (GDN) and Kimi Delta Attention (KDA). Although they compress the context into a fixed-size recurrent state and substantially reduce the cost of long-context processing, repeatedly reading and updating that state remains a major inference bottleneck. Quantization offers a natural way to reduce this cost, but can significantly degrade model quality, due to the accumulation of rounding errors and the presence of outlier rows and columns in the state. To address these challenges, we propose LeapQuant, a training-free method that achieves near-lossless performance under 8-bit recurrent-state quantization. First, to mitigate error accumulation, we propose per-window quantization, which leaps over a window of tokens and quantizes the state only once at its end. Within a window, outputs are computed from the fixed low-bit state together with high-precision buffered updates. Second, to reduce the error introduced by each quantization, LeapQuant retains the state's largest outliers as a few high-precision Compensator Tokens, which share the update path of real tokens. We then smooth the remaining residual before quantization to further reduce the error. Comprehensive experiments across the Qwen, Kimi, and GLM model families show that LeapQuant substantially reduces memory and compute costs during inference. With accuracy comparable to the FP32 baseline, it achieves average speedups of 2.05--3.70$\times$ at the kernel level and 1.47$\times$ for end-to-end inference on NVIDIA B200, RTX PRO 6000, and RTX 5090 GPUs.
candidates.author: Yi Pan, Haocheng Xi, Kan Zhu, Xingyang Li, Yibo Wu, Mayank Mishra, Hongtao Zhang, William X. Zheng, Baris Kasikci, Song Han, Kurt Keutzer, Rishabh Iyer, Ion Stoica

candidates.title: Rho: A Foundation for Efficiently Adaptable VLA Models
candidates.description: General-purpose physical AI models must combine broad visual and linguistic capabilities with precise control across robot embodiments and efficient adaptation to downstream tasks. We introduce Rho, a family of open-weights VLA models for bimanual manipulation designed for data-light task adaptation on 3 embodiments representative of dual-arm robots across research labs and the industry -- YAM Box, UR AI Trainer, and FR3 Duo. We systematically ablate Rho's action-expert architecture and training recipe, and show in controlled simulation and physical-robot experiments that embodiment midtraining improves downstream adaptation. The resulting Rho variants for YAM Box, UR AI Trainer, and FR3 Duo match or outperform existing open-weights VLAs and achieve the strongest overall performance across the tasks, embodiments, and baselines evaluated in this report. We further demonstrate the Rho model family's built-in capacity for online adaptation: an internal latent policy learns from corrective feedback to select observation-conditioned noise inputs for the frozen flow-matching action expert. With as few as 15 corrected episodes, adapting this lightweight module enables Rho to handle task situations at the fringe of its offline finetuning distribution. Together, these results position Rho as both a strong general-purpose robotic manipulation model and a practical foundation for adaptation. We release the base Rho model and the embodiment-specific checkpoints to facilitate Rho's deployment in research experiments and practical industrial use cases.
candidates.author: Rho Team, Simran Bagaria, Daphne Chen, Dean Fortier, Jianlong Fu, Michael Harrison, Tess Hellebrekers, Neel Joshi, Andrey Kolobov, Dalton Moore, Galen Mullins, Michael Murray, Eduardo Salinas, Reuben Tan

candidates.title: Rethinking Representations for World-Action Modeling
candidates.description: World-action models jointly learn robot policies and predict future observations, making the representation space an interface between control and prediction. We study the design of this space through controlled comparisons, finding that neither reconstruction fidelity nor pre-trained perceptual features alone ensure effective policy learning. These findings motivate ReWAM, a representation-centric world-action model built on pre-trained DINO features. Feature Calibration and a Temporal Representation Bottleneck organize these features into compact world states suited to dynamics modeling. Action-Grounded Representation Shaping routes only action-loss gradients to the bottleneck, thereby letting the policy shape what the representation encodes while the world model learns how it evolves. Without generative video pre-training, ReWAM achieves 93.6% success on RoboTwin 2.0. On RoboDojo, it achieves an average score of 12.29 and a success rate of 8.28% using approximately 600 hours of embodied pre-training data.
candidates.author: Haoyi Jiang, Liu Liu, Xinjiang Wang, Zhihao Sun, Zequn Chen, Sen Wang, Xinjie Wang, Xia Chen, Jingfeng Yao, Weiheng Zhao, Shanglin Yuan, Zhizhong Su, Wei Sui, Wenyu Liu, Xinggang Wang

candidates.title: EmoRES-TTS: Residual-Enhanced Vector Steering for Emotional Speech Generation
candidates.description: Emotion-conditioned text-to-speech (TTS) models may fail to express the requested emotion reliably, and improving controllability by additional training is costly in both computation and emotion-labeled speech training data. We therefore study vector steering, a training-free approach that modifies the internal representations of a frozen model. CoCoEmo, a conventional vector steering method for emotion TTS, treats each emotion vector as an indivisible direction controlled by a single global strength, limiting adherence to the requested emotion. In this work, we first discover that an emotion vector can be decomposed into a shared component that moves speech away from neutral expression and a residual component that directs generation toward the requested emotion. Building on this finding, we propose Emotion Residual-Enhanced Steering for TTS (EmoRES), a novel method that controls the two components without retraining the backbone. On IEMOCAP, EmoRES outperforms CoCoEmo across all four objective emotion metrics on the IndexTTS-2 and CosyVoice2 backbones. Rank correlation improves by 26.13 and 12.97 percentage points, corresponding to relative gains of 118.8% and 33.1%, while emotion hit rate improves by 12.95 and 6.92 points, corresponding to relative gains of 20.1% and 9.8%. Human evaluation further shows a relative improvement up to 35.0% in the rate at which listeners correctly identified the dominant requested emotion and up to a 17.3% improvement in fidelity, while listeners prefer EmoRES for naturalness in up to 63.8% of pairwise comparisons. Component ablations further demonstrate that effective control benefits from preserving the shared component while strengthening the residual of the emotion steering vectors.
candidates.author: Kuan-Po Huang, Haohe Liu, Puyuan Peng, Haibin Wu, Zhaoheng Ni, Hung-yi Lee, Jinwon Lee, Neha Chachra

candidates.title: Beyond the Timeline: Augmenting Long-Video Memory with Grounded Entity Biographies
candidates.description: Answering questions about long videos often requires connecting events involving the same objects across hours or days. Chronological descriptions and text-derived entities can leave physical identity unresolved: different objects may share a description, while observations of the same object remain disconnected across events. Retrieving relevant events therefore does not necessarily recover the "biography" of the particular entity a question concerns. To address this, we introduce Grounded Entity Biographies (GEB), a long-video memory framework that groups visually grounded observations of the same physical instance across clips into retrievable biographies while preserving the context of each moment. During question answering, the biography is retrieved alongside episodic evidence, allowing the model to follow an entity through events using identity links established during memory construction. Evaluations across four benchmarks, including day-long and week-long recordings, demonstrate improvements over prior memory frameworks in both multiple-choice and open-ended question answering. On EgoLifeQA, GEB achieves 72.0% accuracy, 4.4 percentage points above the best published result. Ablations show that grounded identity association and biography reading both contribute to the gains, which additional descriptions alone do not fully recover.
candidates.author: Hui Ren, Lei Fan, Henry Pao, Han Guo, Zeeshan Zia, Ying Chen, Alexander Schwing, Gang Hua

candidates.title: Pretraining Latent Information Feedback Transformers with Teacher Supervision
candidates.description: Transformer language models (LMs) are feed-forward: deep-layer representations are never fed back to shallower layers, and the only pathway for information to flow downward across generation steps is the decoded token. This narrow channel forces models to recompute intermediate results and to discard alternative continuations. In this work, we remove this bottleneck during pretraining, introducing the LIFT (Latent Information Feedback Transformer) architecture and training method which enable LMs to propagate state across generation. We achieve this by turning recurrent-state learning into a teacher-forced prediction problem: each input token is paired with an information-dense state, derived from the next-token distribution of an off-the-shelf pretrained LM. The model, extended with a small number of additional parameters, is then trained to predict both the next token and the next state. As the input states are precomputed, pretraining remains fully parallel across positions. At inference, the model's own predicted states are fed back, with a minor computational overhead that decreases with model size. Experiments with pretrained models ranging from 135M to 1B parameters show that LIFT consistently outperforms standard Transformers and baselines on language modeling, downstream reasoning tasks, and procedural tasks under token-matched budget, while being on par with or ahead of compute-matched Transformers. Moreover, a controlled study on a state-tracking task shows that a tiny LIFT outperforms same-size Transformers trained on 8x more data, even when trained with the states of a Transformer that fails the task. Overall, we show that LMs can learn to exploit deep-to-shallow feedback during pretraining via scalable teacher supervision.
candidates.author: Dor Tirosh, Ido Amos, Mor Geva

candidates.title: Thinking Before Thinking: Scaling Agentic Inference Through Meta-Reasoning
candidates.description: As agents take on longer and more complex problems, controlling the execution becomes a task in its own right. Each step in the run brings new control choices, like which partial work to build on, whether to start fresh, or when to stop. We introduce agentic meta-reasoning, an inference-time harness that makes these choices an explicit and structured reasoning process. Workers carry out the task-level computation, while a controller consolidates what the run has established, explores next options, assesses what each option is worth under the remaining budget, and dispatches the chosen work with context drawn from persistent memory. Between decisions the controller carries only a compact account of the run rather than replaying its full history. Our baselines span production coding agents and research harnesses, together with a Direct Control Agent using the same workers and compute budget allowance. On ProgramBench, which tests long-horizon agentic capability through program reconstruction, meta-reasoning achieves 71.5% with GPT-5.5 against 58.0% for Codex; with Opus 4.8 it achieves 67.2% against 65.5% for Claude Code. On the other benchmarks, spanning abstract reasoning, multi-domain long-horizon reasoning, and proof generation, it gains between 3.6 and 4.2 points over direct control, averaged across three frontier models. It keeps improving over the tested budget ranges where direct control plateaus, though its overhead can hurt at small budgets. Artifact-graph analysis reveals more reuse of earlier work, higher coverage of correct solutions in most settings, and nonuniform gains in final selection. These results indicate that spending computation on structured control becomes more important as agents scale to longer runs.
candidates.author: Paras Dahal, Anton Bakhtin, Taco Cohen, Zhengxing Chen, Carole-Jean Wu, Rob Fergus, Scott Yih, Gabriel Synnaeve, Ruslan Salakhutdinov, Sanjeev Arora, Jason Weston, Anirudh Goyal
